newsitem.title: POLAND: Four Polish banks sign merger agreement.
newsitem.headline: Four Polish banks sign merger agreement.

text.p: Four state-owned Polish banks on Monday signed a final agreement merging themselves into a single group led by Pekao SA, the latest step along the road to consolidate and privatise the banking sector.
"The banks will retain their separate indentity...but will implement a common financial policy," deputy Finance Minister Ryszard Pazura said after the signing ceremony.
The privatisation of the group, which controls about 20 percent of Poland's banking service sector, is likely to take place in 1998, Pekao president Andrzej Dorosz told Reuters.
The government programme is designed to strengthen the banking sector before the market is opened to international competition in 1999.
Under the deal, Pekao will receive 100 percent stakes in the three banks by the end of the year, creating Poland's strongest banking group as regards the balance sheet total and own funds.

Apart from Pekao, the group includes Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA, based in the city of Lodz, Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA, based in Lublin and Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA, based in the Baltic port of Szczecin.

The four banks had a balance sheet total of 37 billion zlotys in June 1996 and own funds of nearly two billion zlotys. State-owned PKO BP, the largest savings bank, had a balance sheet total of 33.4 billion. The whole banking system has a total of 180 billion.
